labels.text: Connect your tools to AGI Cloud

S55.01.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with connector access (the screen says Connectors are not available for this account otherwise)
S55.01.note: The state label appears only on connected cards; a catalogue entry that is not connected shows no state text.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud, open Settings, and under the Cloud section tap Connectors.
Read the list of cards. Each card shows the connector name and, when given, the publisher after it (for example Name, Publisher).
Tap the Search connectors box at the bottom only to confirm the list is not empty; a connected card shows Connected with a date.
Compare with Expected: each entry shows name, publisher and state. Connectors that are not connected show no state label, only the name and publisher.
S55.01.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors. The screen opens with the title Connectors and the line Connect your tools to AGI Cloud. Each card shows name and publisher.

S55.02.note: On the phone, the filter for connected cards matches name, publisher and description only, not tool names; the catalogue search is sent to the server, and whether it matches tool names could not be confirmed from the app code.
steps: Open Settings > Cloud > Connectors and note the names of a few cards.
Tap the Search connectors box at the bottom and type part of a connector name you saw.
Watch the list: only matching cards should remain.

Clear the box, then type a publisher name or a word from a description, and check that matching cards appear. Then type a tool name (for example one you saw on a connector detail page) and compare with Expected.
S55.02.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Search connectors box at the bottom of the screen.

S55.03.needs: none beyond the Connectors screen; a category chip appears only when the directory has connectors in that category
S55.03.note: The category list comes from the shared contracts; chips for categories with no listings are hidden, so not every category is always shown.
steps: Open Settings > Cloud > Connectors.
Look at the row of chips: All and Connected are always there. Scroll the row sideways to find category chips such as Productivity.
Tap a category chip such as Productivity.
Compare with Expected: the list should show only connectors in that category. Tap All to return to the full list.
S55.03.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > the row of filter chips under the Add custom MCP box (chips All, Connected, Custom, and category names).

S55.04.note: Link rows appear only when the connector has that URL; the tools list appears only when the connector lists tools.
steps: Open Settings > Cloud > Connectors and tap a connector card that is not connected.
Read the name, the line By (publisher), and the description under it.
Check the row Sign-in (its value is Account sign-in, API key, Not needed or Checked on connect).
Scroll to What it can do and the link rows Documentation, Website, Support and Privacy policy. Compare with Expected: description, publisher, sign-in requirement, tools and links.
S55.04.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connector card. The detail screen shows the name, By publisher, the description, the Sign-in row, What it can do, and the link rows.

S55.07.needs: a connector that is not connected and is released (Coming soon connectors have no Connect button); for a real sign-in step, an outside account for that provider
S55.07.note: Connect is hidden for connectors that are Coming soon or whose setup is on desktop or CLI only; the alert text comes from a shared contracts function.
steps: Open a connector that is not connected and shows the Connect button (not Coming soon).
Tap Connect.
In the alert titled Connect [name]?, read the text and tap Allow (or Deny to stop).
Compare with Expected: after Allow, the real sign-in or key step starts (a browser or in-app sign-in page for an account sign-in connector, or the API key form for an API key connector).
S55.07.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connector that is not connected > Connect.

S55.08.needs: an outside account for that provider (the account to approve the grant)
S55.08.note: If the sign-in page is closed before finishing, the app shows an alert saying the connector is not connected yet; the grant is stored by the server, which the app code does not show directly.
steps: Open a connector whose Sign-in row says Account sign-in and tap Connect.
Tap Allow in the alert Connect [name]?.
Wait for the provider's own consent page to open (in the app browser or the in-app sign-in sheet) and approve it there.

Return to the app and compare with Expected: the connector should now show Connected with a date under the Connected filter, and its detail page should show Connected to AGI Cloud and a Granted access section.
S55.08.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connector whose Sign-in row reads Account sign-in > Connect > Allow.

S55.09.needs: an API key for that provider
S55.09.note: The form opens only when the server asks for credentials; otherwise the connector may connect straight after Allow. Whether the key is stored encrypted is not visible in the UI.
steps: Open a connector whose Sign-in row says API key and tap Connect, then Allow.
In the form, tap the API key box (placeholder API key) and type a key.
Tap Test and save.
Compare with Expected: a bad key shows an error and nothing is saved; a good key closes the form and the detail page shows Connected to AGI Cloud. The encryption cannot be seen from the screen.
S55.09.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connector whose Sign-in row reads API key > Connect > Allow > API key form.

S55.17.needs: a connected connector (a connector that has granted permissions or scopes)
S55.17.note: The section is hidden when the connection reports neither permission sentences nor scopes.
steps: Open a connector that is connected (it shows a Connected date on the list).
On its detail page, read the Connected to AGI Cloud heading and the rows under it.
Find the Granted access section: each row shows a permission sentence and the word Read or Write.
If no sentence rows appear, look for a Granted access row listing scope names. Compare with Expected: the permissions shown should be what was granted.
S55.17.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connected connector > Connected to AGI Cloud > Granted access section.

S55.18.needs: a connected connector; the not-responding and expired states depend on the provider and cannot be set up from the app
S55.18.note: The word healthy is not shown; a healthy connector shows Connected with a date on the list and no warning box.
steps: Open Settings > Cloud > Connectors and read the state text on each connected card: Connected [date] means healthy; Not responding is amber; Authorization expired, reconnect is red.
Tap a connected card. Read the warning boxes: Not responding (with Check again), Authorization expired, or Needs to be reconnected.
Scroll to the section Connection health and read its state and summary text, or Not called in the last hour.
Compare with Expected: each connector shows whether it is healthy, needs reauthorization or is not responding.
S55.18.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors: the state text on each card. On a connector detail page: the Not responding box, Authorization expired, and the Connection health card.

S55.20.needs: an account-sign-in (OAuth) connector whose grant has expired or been revoked, and an outside account for that provider
S55.20.note: The top Reconnect card appears only for account-sign-in connectors whose grant expired; API key connectors show Replace API key instead.
steps: Use a connector whose authorization has expired or been revoked (it shows Authorization expired, reconnect on the list).
On the Connectors screen, look for the card at the top and tap Reconnect; or tap the connector and scroll to the Authorization expired box.
Tap Reauthorize on the detail page.
Compare with Expected: the provider's authorization page should open for the same connector, and after approval the state should change to Connected.
S55.20.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors: a card at the top with a Reconnect button, or a connector detail page with Reauthorize (under Authorization expired).

S55.22.needs: a connected connector you can reconnect afterwards
S55.22.note: The effect on the assistant is not shown on the connector screens; it is an inner behaviour of the server and the chat.
steps: Open a connected connector and scroll to the bottom of its detail page.
Tap Disconnect. Read the alert Disconnect [name]? and its text about saved tool permissions.
Tap Disconnect in the alert.
Compare with Expected: the screen returns to Connectors and the connector no longer shows as connected. Whether the assistant still uses it is not shown on this screen; check it in a chat if needed.
S55.22.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connected connector > scroll to the bottom > Disconnect > Disconnect (in the alert).

S55.23.needs: a connected connector, and an outside account for the provider to check the provider side
S55.23.note: No Revoke wording exists in the mobile connector screens or services/connectors.ts (searched rg -i revoke in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors and services/connectors.ts). The nearest control is Disconnect, whose alert does not say the provider token is revoked; whether the provider is asked to revoke is not shown in mobile code.

S55.25.note: No folder or repository selection for a connector was found in apps/mobile (searched rg -i for repositor and folder in apps/mobile/src and app, filtered for connector, mcp, scope, github and drive). Only unrelated hits came back, such as GitHub repository URLs in the cloud code session sheet and src/features/settings/code/GitHubConnections.tsx, which was not checked as a connector control.

S55.27.needs: a connected connector that has write tools
S55.27.note: The group-level level is read from the saved settings but the app only sends changes per tool, so there is no visible control to set all write tools at once; the global Action approvals row on the Connectors screen is a separate setting.
steps: Open a connected connector that has write tools and scroll to Tool permissions.
Find the group heading Write and delete tools and read the tool rows under it.
Tap Allow, Ask or Block on one write tool (Allow runs it automatically, Ask asks first, Block stops it).
Compare with Expected: the row should show the chosen level. Tap the reset control on a row (Reset [tool] to default) to return it to the default, which follows Action approvals.
S55.27.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > tap a connected connector > Tool permissions > Write and delete tools > tap a tool's Allow, Ask or Block choice.
